column2: Retain Saba's queen hearing Solomon's name, testing with riddles, the large entourage and camel cargo, and everything in her soul. No additional Lord-name qualification is imported from Kings.
Retain answering all her questions and the negative that no matter escaped explanation. Questions and matter contextually render the repeated word noun without adding a new category of test.
Retain the queen seeing wisdom and the built house. The observation list continues into the next unit before its resulting reaction.

Retain table food, servants' seating, ministers' standing and clothing, wine-pourers' attire and burnt offerings, followed by being beside herself. Do not replace the selected offerings with a stairway or ascent.
Retain the truth of the report heard in her own land about words and wisdom. Ordinary your addresses Solomon, not God.

Retain disbelief until personal sight, explicit behold, not half the abundance of wisdom reported and surpassing the report. The half comparison is not replaced with the different selected wording in 1 Kings.
Retain happy men and these happy servants who continually stand and hear. The initial men has no supplied your possessive; the servants do.

Retain blessing of Solomon's God, placement on His throne as king for God, divine love for Israel and judgment and righteousness. The throne belongs to God in this selected speech, and Israel is the contextual object of enduring establishment.
Retain 120 gold talents, abundant spices, precious stones and the unmatched spices statement. The comparison concerns these spices, not an added measure of all earlier royal wealth.
Retain both Solomon's and Chiram's servants, gold from Souphir, pinewood and precious stones. This begins a narrative aside without making the queen donor of these separate imports.

Retain pinewood stairways for both houses and kitharas and nablas for singers, with no previous likeness seen in Judah. The technical instrument forms and selected stairways remain provisional rather than harmonized to supports.

Retain everything requested, apart from all she had brought and her return to her land. Do not change the gifts comparison to gifts according to royal generosity or add a departing servant group absent here.
column3: The relation of apart from to the reciprocal gifts is unresolved; no exact exchange value is claimed.

column2: Retain one year's 666 gold talents. No symbolic interpretation or present-day valuation is inserted into the reading.

Retain additional receipts from subjected men and merchants, and gold/silver from Arabian kings and land satraps. The selected subjected men are not silently converted into a different merchant class.
Retain 200 large hammered-gold shields and both statements of 600 gold pieces per shield. The repetition is selected and is not deleted as a copying error.
column3: Gold pieces is provisional for the substantival gold term; no specific shekel or coin denomination is established.

column2: Retain 300 shields, 300 gold pieces each and the House of the Forest of Lebanon. The different shield noun and quantity remain distinct from the large shields.
Retain the ivory throne's explicit tusk wording and tested-gold covering. The apparent material repetition remains source-led rather than silently shortened.
Retain six steps fastened with gold, paired armrests and two lions. No separate gold footstool or unexpressed round back is imported.
Retain twelve lions on six steps, on either side, and uniqueness among kingdoms. No assumption about a total including the two armrest lions replaces the stated figures.
Retain all royal vessels as gold and forest-house vessels covered with gold, with silver of no account. The two gold constructions remain distinct rather than asserting solid gold for every object.
Retain a ship going to Tharsis, ships returning every three years and gold, silver, elephant tusks and apes. The singular/plural change is selected; no peacocks are added.
Retain Solomon surpassing all kings in both wealth and wisdom. No additional geographic restriction is inserted into this comparative statement.
Retain all earth's kings seeking his presence to hear God-given heart wisdom. The divine source of wisdom remains distinct from the visiting rulers' activity.
Retain each annual gift, silver and gold vessels, clothing, stacte, aromatics, horses and mules. Do not replace stacte with armor from a parallel list.
column3: Stacte remains provisional technical perfumery vocabulary requiring lexical review.

column2: Retain 4,000 female horses for chariots and 12,000 horsemen with their locations. Mares reflects the selected sex designation; no horse stalls or 40,000 figure is substituted.
Retain leadership of all kings from the River to foreign territory and Egypt's border. The River remains unnamed within this unit rather than receiving an unexpressed proper name.
Retain both gold and silver like stones and abundant cedars like plain sycamores. No absent Judea phrase is copied from chapter 1.
Retain horses coming from Egypt and all the land. The second source is not narrowed to one named trading region.
Retain first and last records, behold, Nathan, Achia the Selonite and Joel the seer concerning Jeroboam. Do not emend Joel to Iddo from another tradition.
Retain forty years over all Israel. No separate regnal subdivision is added.
Retain Solomon's sleep, burial by unnamed plural agents in his father's city and Rehoboam's succession. Do not add with his fathers to the selected shorter sleep clause.
Retain Rehoboam's arrival at Sychem and all Israel coming there to make him king. The repeated city anchors both actions.
Retain Jeroboam hearing, the Egyptian residence and flight parenthesis, and return from Egypt. Repeated names and Egypt references remain, and the return is not changed to continued residence.
Retain the summons and Jeroboam with the entire assembly approaching Rehoboam. The sending subject remains unexpressed rather than newly identified as a particular council.
Retain harsh yoke, harsh bondage and heavy burden, with promised service after relief. The yoke image is not reduced to taxation alone.
Retain the three-day dismissal and return command, followed by the people's departure. The stated timing is preserved for the third-day return later.
Retain the elders who served Solomon during his life and the question about an answer to the people. No counsel content is anticipated before the next unit.
Retain today's goodness, favor and good words, with continuing service as the result. Do not replace this advice with a different servanthood formulation from Kings.
Retain abandonment of the elders' counsel and consultation with peers raised alongside the king and serving before him. Their upbringing and current position both explain the group.
Retain his request for advice and the repeated people's plea to relax the father's yoke. The repetition links the competing councils rather than providing a new complaint.
Retain the repeated instructions, the quoted demand for release and the explicit little finger thicker than paternal loins. Ordinary you remains in the nested human-address quotations.

Propose restoring Now at the opening to represent the selected and-now discourse turn omitted from the inherited line. Retain the father disciplining with a heavy yoke, addition to the yoke and the contrast of whips and scorpions. The close stage preserves the inherited unmarked opening; no literal-animal explanation is added.

Retain Jeroboam and all the people returning on the third day with the king's repeated third-day instruction. The narrative confirms the scheduled return rather than changing it to three complete days later.
Retain the harsh answer and repeated rejection of elders' counsel, continuing into the younger advisers' wording. The explicit King Rehoboam remains despite the preceding king reference.
Retain the actual answer's heavy yoke and added burden, then whips/scorpions. The selected speech here does not repeat the little-finger boast, so it is not imported from the advice.
Retain non-listening, divine reversal and the saying clause about the Lord establishing His word through Achia concerning Jeroboam. The quotation and grammatical object continue into verse 16.
column3: The attachment of saying and the inferred quotation boundary remain unresolved; reversal is not rewritten as a purpose clause from another witness.

column2: Retain and all Israel as completion of the prior concerning phrase, the repeated non-listening explanation and the people's rejection of Davidic share/inheritance. Dwellings, house and final departure remain; no missing Israel-saw clause is inserted.
column3: The opening genitive and clause linkage remain source-specific and difficult; the inherited quotation punctuation is provisional.

column2: Retain Israelite men living in Judah's cities under Rehoboam. Their location, not a newly asserted exclusive tribal identity, distinguishes this group.
Retain Adoniram over tribute, stoning with stones and death, then Rehoboam's hurried chariot escape to Jerusalem. The repetitions and selected name remain, without softening the killing.
column3: Tribute in this administrative context may involve compulsory labor; the precise office remains under review.

column2: Retain Israel's rejection of David's house to this day. Allegiance is an inherited contextual complement of the rejection verb, not a separately expressed Greek noun.
